title: Ardas in joy
hookLine: births, weddings and new homes all get an Ardas of thanks

lines: GOOD NEWS GETS AN ARDAS TOO.
cards: When do you reach for something bigger more often: when things are falling apart, or when they're going well? Trouble tends to send people looking. Good news tends to go to the group chat.
Sikh life has a deliberate counterweight. A baby is born: an Ardas. A wedding: an Ardas at the start and at the end.
A new home, a new shop, a new job that finally came through: an Ardas. Not asking for anything. Just saying thank you.

teach.b: Punjabi has a word for this: shukrana, thanksgiving. A shukrane di ardas is a prayer of thanks, the same frame as every Ardas, with the petition turned into gratitude. Look at how joy gets marked.
When a baby is born, the family often brings the child to the gurdwara.

teach.h: A BIRTH: A NAME FROM THE HUKAM.
teach.b: An Ardas of thanks is said, the Guru Granth Sahib is opened at random, and the first letter of the hymn on that page, the hukamnama, guides the choice of the child's name.

teach.h: A WEDDING BEGINS AND ENDS IN ARDAS.
teach.b: A wedding, the Anand Karaj, begins with an Ardas; the couple walks around the Guru Granth Sahib four times, and it ends with an Ardas again.
In a new home, many families hold a reading, often of Sukhmani Sahib, and close it with an Ardas, sometimes with karah prashad for everyone who came.
You'll often hear Anand Sahib too, the song of bliss by Guru Amar Das, on ang 917. It opens, in effect: joy has come, my mother, for I have found the True Guru.
The Rehat Maryada has it sung at weddings and other ceremonies, and a short portion is recited near the close of congregational gatherings.

Why make such a point of thanks? In Sikh teaching, the good things are gifts from the One just as surely as the hard things are within the Will. Grief is met with acceptance; joy is met with gratitude.
Both keep the eyes on the Giver, not only on the gift.

how: Sikhs mark births, weddings, new homes and other blessings with a shukrana, an Ardas of thanks, often with a reading, karah prashad and the singing of Anand Sahib.

games.q: your family just moved into a new home. what do Sikh families often do first?
o: throw a party and skip the formalities.
hold a reading and an Ardas of thanks.
wait a year to see if it works out.
games.why: often a reading of Sukhmani Sahib, closed with a shukrana Ardas and karah prashad for everyone who came.

practice: Find one joy from the last week, a good meal, a text from an old friend, a morning when your knee didn't ache, and bring it back as clearly as you can: where you were, who was there. Instead of moving on, stay with it.
If you pray, you can thank the One for it in your own words or with a single Waheguru; if not, simply hold the gratitude without asking for anything more.

wordCard.voice: Shukrana, thanksgiving: births, weddings, new homes and answered hopes all get one, an Ardas of thanks, often with Anand Sahib, the song of bliss.
